question.text: When a mutual fund scheme undergoes a fundamental attribute change (such as change in investment objective or scheme type), what right does the investor have?

answer.text: Right to vote against the change at a unitholder meeting
Right to exit the scheme without any exit load within a prescribed period after being notified of the change
Right to switch to any other AMC's scheme at no cost
Right to receive additional units as compensation for the change

explanation.text: The Logic: When a scheme's fundamental attributes are changed, existing investors must be notified and given the right to exit the scheme without any exit load within the prescribed time period. This protects investors who no longer wish to remain in a scheme whose character has materially changed. The Trap: The right tested here is the load-free exit within the prescribed period; the option about voting or blocking the change is not the right the source emphasises in this context. Note: Source: NISM Series II-B (RTA Mutual Fund) workbook references the notification and load-free exit window for fundamental attribute changes.
